text:
🇲🇽🌎 <u>UN orders Mexico to find a young worker taken in Ensenada</u>

The UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances registered urgent action 2388/2026 for Jesús Alexandro Sánchez Gerardo, 24, and asked the Mexican state for immediate measures to find him. On August 20, armed men who identified themselves as Ensenada municipal police pulled him and two coworkers from company dormitories with threats and beatings, per the Cedhapi human rights center. He hasn't been seen since.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>"On Saturdays, no brown people get in"</u>

Audios attributed to Strana, a nightclub in San Pedro Garza García — Mexico's richest municipality — have a staffer asking whether anyone in a group is "de piel morena o negra," because dark-skinned people don't get in on Saturdays. "Sé que suena racista. Porque sí es racista. Así es en Strana." Nuevo León's anti-discrimination council announced an inspection. As Ana María Ibarra writes in Contralínea, almost nobody needed proof to believe it: in 2022 CDMX found Sonora Grill guilty of segregating diners by appearance.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>The UN's refugee chief comes to study Mexico's model</u>

UNHCR's Barham Salih is in Mexico on his first visit, and the Senate receives him Tuesday in a solemn session for the 75th anniversary of the Refugee Convention. The agenda: strengthen Mexico's asylum system and its national integration network. Since 2019 Mexico has registered more than 600,000 asylum applicants — one of the top receiving countries on earth — and 240 companies have already hired refugees.
